text: **A GENERATED VIEW MUST BE A FIXED POINT OF THE PROJECT'S FORMATTER: the render output survives the formatter unchanged, or the skew check oscillates forever.** (vc 2026-08-19, settling cc's AC-00.10 hand-off. Mechanism established WITHOUT rendering, then confirmed by accident.) **THE RENDERER IS PROVABLY INCAPABLE OF CAUSING THIS.** `criterion_line` (`views.rs:463`) is `format!("- {} ", c.id)` + an optional `(non-test) ` + `push_str(&c.text)` VERBATIM; `finish()` (`:217`) only pops trailing newlines and appends the footer. `cell()` -- the escaper -- is not on this path at all. So the renderer does not merely fail to collapse whitespace, **it never operates on the string.** **THE DISCRIMINATOR IS INLINE CODE SPAN VERSUS PROSE, AND IT IS A MECHANISM ARGUMENT RATHER THAN A CORRELATION: A RENDERER-SIDE COLLAPSE CANNOT BE BACKTICK-SENSITIVE; A MARKDOWN FORMATTER NECESSARILY IS, because backtick spans are exactly what it must not reflow.** Canon-wide the population is three double spaces: ST0056 AC-00.10 x2, both prose at a `**bold**  **bold**` boundary -- EATEN; ST0050 AC-01.1 x1, inside `` `  - [ ] NN: title` `` -- SURVIVED. **THE CONFOUND WAS EXCLUDED AT ONE REVISION RATHER THAN ASSUMED:** at `54735e34` canon carried 2 and the committed view carried 0, and that same commit regenerated ST0050's view in the same 263-view sweep. **Same commit, same pipeline, same file kind, same `- AC-XX.Y` construct: one eaten, one survived. ST0050 is a CONTROL, not a counterexample.** **CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS WHY THE INSTANCE IS NOT THE FIX: `doctor` reported 263 skew going to 0 across that commit, so its zero was TRUE WHEN TAKEN AND FALSE BY THE TIME IT WAS COMMITTED.** Generate two spaces, formatter collapses to one, skew check sees drift, regenerate two spaces -- forever, **with every pass looking like a legitimate repair.** **SECOND INSTANCE OF A PAIR THE CODEBASE ALREADY DOCUMENTS AND ALREADY FIXED ONCE:** `views.rs`'s own `kv()` comment records emitting `key:` with no trailing space because prettier strips trailing whitespace and the two would *oscillate forever* -- **found by running the real formatter.** The remedy there is the remedy here: make the RENDERER emit what the formatter would leave alone. **Repairing AC-00.10's text is the trap -- it looks like a repair and leaves the loop.** **EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED 2026-08-19 by an experiment nobody was willing to run:** cc's accidental `intent upgrade` regenerated `ST0056/acceptance.md` carrying **2** double spaces against the committed file's **0**. Renderer emits, formatter eats. **The finding was already established by mechanism; this removed the last doubt.** **REMEDY CLAUSE WITHDRAWN 2026-08-19 (cc measured it; vc ruled), AND THE PROPERTY SURVIVES IN A STRONGER FORM.** This row prescribed _make the RENDERER emit what the formatter would leave alone_, and that remedy CONTRADICTS THIS ROW'S OWN MECHANISM ARGUMENT stated three sentences earlier -- _the renderer does not merely fail to collapse whitespace, it never operates on the string_. **The row refuted itself, which is AC-11.1's class committed by the row that names a second writer.** **cc BUILT THE PRESCRIBED REMEDY AND THE POPULATION REFUSED IT: over 6,095 authored lines a conservative renderer-side rule produced EIGHT changes where the real formatter makes SEVEN.** The extra is ST0056 AC-10.9, whose prose runs backticks straight into words, so the real parser's code-span boundaries fall where no hand-rolled segmenter can see them -- **and rewriting a site the formatter leaves alone is the same oscillation with the arrow reversed, invisible to anything short of running the real formatter.** **AND IT WAS ALREADY FORBIDDEN IN WRITING: `view_determinism.rs:248` records that authored prose passes the renderer VERBATIM by rule, because `migration.md` forbids reflowing it -- so normalising markup in the renderer is the one thing the renderer may not do.** That constraint predates both nodes looking, and it also named the structural fix and declined to take it unilaterally. **THE RULED REMEDY IS D02 APPLIED TO WRITERS RATHER THAN TO CONTENT: A GENERATED VIEW HAS ONE WRITER AND IT IS THE RENDERER.** The cause was never an output form -- `.git/hooks/pre-commit` runs `prettier --write` over every staged markdown file and `git add`s its own rewrite, so all 266 generated views had a second writer and a silent one. Closed by `.prettierignore` at `91380693`. **SO THE DURABLE PROPERTY IS ONE WRITER AND FIXED-POINT-NESS WAS THE SYMPTOM: a fixed point is a coincidence somebody must maintain forever; an exclusion is structural.** **DEMONSTRATED LIVE RATHER THAN STAGED: vc synced mid-session with the exclusion in place and the regenerated view came back carrying canon's `*KIND*` against HEAD's `_KIND_`, all seven divergences gone.**
